title.narrative: Building Sustainable Futures: Science Diplomacy in the Maghreb

description.narrative:
Our planet is heading toward global warming beyond 1.5°C by 2100, surpassing the Paris Agreement target. Climate‑change disruptions — droughts, floods, storms, and heatwaves — are already intensifying. Yet, research output in critical sustainability areas remains limited. In this fragile landscape, science diplomacy emerges as a bridge between science, policy, and society, offering tools to foster cooperation and evidence‑based decision‑making across borders.
Science diplomacy sits at the intersection of science and foreign policy, offering a framework to address global challenges such as climate change, human rights, and sustainable development. While rooted in long‑standing practices of international cooperation, it was only formally conceptualized in 2010.
Objectives: 1. Advance peace and human rights by embedding scientific expertise into policy dialogue. 2. Promote sustainable development through evidence‑based decision‑making. 3. Consolidate science diplomacy capacity at global, regional, and national levels. 4. Align efforts with the 2025 UNESCO Global Ministerial Dialogue to set strategic direction.
The workplan will contribute the following key activities: - Generate the evidence and analysis Member States need to act across the priority areas, building a stronger shared evidence base; - Support Member States and regional and continental organizations in shaping their own science diplomacy strategies, so that more of them have strategies to act on; -Broaden partnerships and access to shared scientific cooperation and infrastructures, widening participation in research no single state can sustain alone; - Convene dialogue at the global and regional levels, sustaining political engagement over time.
